edges.description: UNC80 is one of two auxiliary subunits required for the channelosome, and the three subunits depend on one another for protein-level stability, so losing UNC80 destabilises the complex.

UNC80 and UNC79 tether to the cytoplasmic loops of NALCN, and two of those interactions are what drive the channel to the cell surface; a C-terminal UNC80 domain additionally overcomes a soma-retention signal to place the channel in dendrites.
edges.target: Loss of NALCN Surface and Dendritic Targeting

edges.description: A third UNC79-UNC80 interaction normally pulls NALCN's auto-inhibitory CIH helix out of its binding site; without UNC80 that relief does not happen and the channel remains self-inhibited.
UNC79 and UNC80 are required for robust NALCN current in heterologous systems, so a destabilised complex conducts less.
Co-expression of UNC79 and UNC80 markedly increases NALCN at the cell surface, and the current rises with it.
edges.source: Loss of NALCN Surface and Dendritic Targeting

edges.description: Unrelieved auto-inhibition keeps the channel in a closed state.
The NALCN leak current is a principal determinant of the neuronal resting membrane potential, so reducing it hyperpolarises and destabilises the resting potential.
Reduced basal excitability of central motor circuits is the proposed explanation for the universal congenital hypotonia.
Altered resting potential across developing cortical and subcortical circuits is the proposed basis of the global delay.
No affected individual develops expressive speech, attributed to the same diffuse excitability defect.
Excess involuntary limb movement is attributed to altered excitability in basal ganglia and related motor circuits.

Seizures occur in a minority and their relationship to a loss of leak conductance is unresolved, since reduced excitability would not obviously predispose to seizures. Reported frequency differs sharply between series.

NALCN-complex loss disrupts brainstem respiratory rhythm in animals, and central sleep apnea is reported in one UNC80 sibling pair. The largest UNC80 cohort nonetheless recorded no breathing abnormality, so this edge is contested and both sides are cited.
Inadequate oral intake from poor suck and dysphagia contributes to the universal failure to thrive, which is why assisted nutrition is a mainstay of management.
A true null allele of the orthologous gene, confirmed by absence of UNC80 protein in mutant brain lysate.
edges.limitations: Neonatal lethality means the model cannot represent the chronic human course, in which most children survive years with severe static impairment. It is a model of the molecular lesion, not of the disease trajectory.

nodes.description: A knock-in of the kind of C-terminal truncation found in affected individuals. Homozygotes are born at close to the expected Mendelian ratio but none survives beyond P1, again with severe apnea. The informative result is electrophysiological: the sodium leak current in cultured mutant neurons is not reduced but significantly larger than wild type, while the truncated UNC80 protein is confined to the soma and absent from axons and dendrites.
Constitutive UNC80 knockout. Pups appear normal at birth but none survives beyond 24 hours, with severe apnea, phenocopying the NALCN knockout.
